reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern for this channel is predominantly flat (zero-slope) with near-zero robust-standardized values, exhibiting extreme stability and no discernible periodicity beyond the estimated period of 4 (which is not visually evident in the flat segments). Three candidates (indices 1, 2, and part of 3) show perfectly constant baselines: reference 1 and 2 are exactly zero over 12 points (3 cycles), while reference 0 is a constant -2.257 over 4 points (1 cycle). Reference 3 contains a sharp, symmetric V-shaped dip centered at index 2544, spanning ~6 points (≈1.5 cycles), dropping from baseline (~-2.26) to -2.26 + 2.257 ≈ 0.0 then returning—this appears to be a transient step-like anomaly rather than normal behavior, as it violates the otherwise universal flatness and zero roughness across other candidates. Amplitude is effectively zero in reliable candidates; any non-zero amplitude (e.g., 2.257 in ref 3) is anomalous. Peaks/troughs are absent in normal segments; when present (ref 3), they are abrupt, high-magnitude, and non-repeating. Noise is negligible (MAD = 0 in all catalog entries), indicating clean, deterministic behavior. Acceptable variation includes minor baseline offsets (e.g., -2.257 vs 0), but only if the segment remains perfectly flat—any slope, curvature, or excursion breaks normality. The consensus normal morphology is a noiseless, zero-roughness, constant-level segment, regardless of absolute level.
